section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a study that investigated the relationship between individual factors (IQ, latent inhibition, schizotypal personality traits) and social factors (social network size) on real-life creative accomplishment in 111 Central-Eastern European volunteers. The study found that IQ and primary social network size independently predicted creative achievements. The text also provides background on the theoretical importance of both individual cognitive abilities and social networks in creativity, highlighting a gap in the literature that this study aimed to address.
